does: Cooks fatty pork in a little liquid until the liquid boils away and the rendered fat is left, then fries the tender meat in that fat until brown and crisp at the edges.
how: Cook chunks of a fatty cut in a little liquid, uncovered, until tender.
Keep cooking as the liquid boils away; the fat that has melted out stays in the pot.
Once the pot sizzles instead of bubbling, let the chunks fry, turning them only now and then.
Stop when they are deep brown and crisp at the edges and still soft inside.

cues.text: The soft bubbling of liquid turns into the crackle of frying.
Brown, crisp edges on soft, juicy meat.
The pieces crunch at the edge under a spoon.

mistakes.mistake: Stirring constantly, which breaks the meat up before it browns.
mistakes.fix: Leave it still to brown, and turn it only now and then.

mistakes.mistake: Letting the pot run dry before the meat is tender.
mistakes.fix: Add a splash of water and keep going until it is tender, then let it boil away.

variant_of.differs: The pot is left uncovered so that the liquid boils away, and the meat ends by frying in its own rendered fat.
